target_customer: Startups and tech companies hiring engineers who want to see how candidates work with AI tools
problem: Standard coding tests no longer show how candidates perform when using AI tools. Litmus generates async assessments from a company's own repos and tickets and grades the process and output.
business_model: B2B SaaS with custom pricing; integrates with Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever

founders.name: Shaivi Rau
founders.background_notes: YC page says early stage startups and VC experience advising founders on which engineers to trust; employer names not given.

founders.name: Elena Zhao
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at Two Sigma and Meta per YC page.

competitors.name: HackerRank
competitors.traction_then: Widely used; comparison pages say about 20 USD per attempt

competitors.name: CodeSignal
competitors.what: Assessments and technical interviews with AI interviewer models
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor listed as close alternative

competitors.name: Karat
competitors.what: Live technical assessments with human interview engineers and AI assistance

technical_complexity.rationale: Sandboxed assessments generated from company context with deterministic harnesses and LLM graders is standard engineering with some hard evaluation design.

defensibility.rationale: Assessment data and grading calibration may compound, but incumbents like HackerRank and CodeSignal are adding AI features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already marketing AI interview and AI proctoring features in 2026.

market_need_then: AI tools made leaked-question coding tests less informative, and hiring teams sought new signals; company reports 3,000 assessments evaluated and about 60k USD ARR.

branding.name_origin: Not stated by a source; a litmus test is a quick decisive check, which the name may allude to
branding.domain_note: Uses litmushiring.com since litmus.com is taken by an email marketing company

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative real word but shared with several unrelated Litmus companies and the similar Lytmus hiring startup, which makes search confusing.

outcome_analysis: Litmus is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It reports early traction with companies like Mercor and Astranis and about 60k USD ARR per its YC page. The risks are well funded incumbent assessment vendors and a name shared with several other Litmus and Lytmus companies.
notes: No funding found. Dealroom lists a 125k USD seed, unverified. The failure factor brand_confusion is a forward looking risk flag, not an observed failure. Reported traction and ARR are company statements on its YC page. Founder education not found.
